#schema: # Install routes per tool, and the routes that are deliberately excluded.
# Six tab-separated fields, one route per record, several records per tool, in
# preference order. The reader takes the first record for a tool whose OS
# matches uname -s and whose probe succeeds, which is what makes "exactly one
# command in a report" fall out of the data rather than out of reporter logic.
#   1 tool      [A-Za-z0-9._-]+. The union of this column is the closed set of
#               tool names a skills/<name>/requires.tsv record may name in its
#               first field, so a declaration cannot introduce a new executable
#               name without a reviewed edit to this file.
#   2 route     Route identifier, printed in the no-route enumeration.
#   3 os        any, darwin, or linux, matched against uname -s.
#   4 probe     Availability test, as <driver> or <driver> <verb>. `tsuku
#               tsuku-info` means tsuku resolves and `tsuku info <tool>`
#               succeeds; `brew -` means brew resolves. `never` marks an
#               excluded route. The verb vocabulary is closed and lives in the
#               reader, so adding a driver is a code change, not a data change.
#   5 command   Emitted verbatim if this record wins. `-` when excluded.
#   6 citation  Issue reference, or `-`. Mandatory and non-dash on any record
#               whose probe is `never`, enforced by the reader.
# Ownership rule: a route is added or excluded together with the incident that
# justifies it, cited by issue number in field six. An excluded route is a
# record rather than an absence on purpose -- it has to appear in the no-route
# enumeration a report prints, with its reason, or a reader concludes the
# maintainers forgot about it.

# jq, git, and python3 are the independent-cadence tools of
# references/tool-declaration-policy.md. They are routed here because the
# declaration reader rejects any field-one value absent from this column, and
# the skills call all three. The commands below are the ones this repo already
# proves: check-plan-scripts.yml, check-execute-scripts.yml, and run-evals.yml
# install jq with exactly these two lines, so the route table repeats what CI
# does rather than inventing a third way. No tsuku route is claimed for any of
# the three -- none is known to resolve under `tsuku info`, and a route that
# guesses is worse than one that is absent.
# git and python3 are effectively always present on a developer host: git
# because a shirabe skill only ever runs inside a checkout, python3 because
# both macOS and every CI image ship it and two scripts use it as the portable
# realpath. Their routes are therefore near-unreachable in practice, and that
# is the point -- an absent-tool block still names one real command instead of
# saying it does not know.
